exposure: traditional laparoscopic myomectomy with barbed sutures
robotic-assisted laparoscopic myomectomy with barbed sutures
cohort: 78 women with symptomatic uterine myomas who underwent either robotic-assisted laparoscopic myomectomy (RALM) with barbed sutures or traditional laparoscopic myomectomy (TLM) with barbed sutures between July 2012 and March 2016
finding: Although RALM had longer surgical time, it did not show a significant decrease in postoperative abdominal drainage compared with TLM, suggesting that barbed sutures in TLM might diminish the superiority of RALM in reducing postoperative blood loss.
